column3: Near-verbatim parallel: messengers are sent only as bearers of good news and warners.
The nearby worldly-life parable provides the broader warning context of this passage.
The preceding declaration of truth and warning of the Fire frames the disbelievers addressed here.
Directly states that messengers are bearers of good news and warnings.
Immediate predecessor: it identifies people as especially prone to disputation.
The local conclusion affirms Allah as the true authority, but does not address false disputation.
It likewise limits the sending of signs to warning and recalls earlier peoples' denial.
Its contrast between worldly adornment and lasting deeds is only a local contextual link.
Direct parallel: those who argue against God have a futile argument before their Lord.
Near-verbatim parallel: disbelieving communities dispute falsely to dislodge the truth.
Immediate predecessor: it explains persistent refusal of guidance and expectation of punishment.
The casting-of-lots narrative uses related wording but has no thematic link.
Directly repeats the consequence of disbelief and treating Allah's signs and messengers as mockery.
The gathering at judgment supplies a broad warning consequence only.
It portrays unbelievers disputing the Hour while believers recognize its truth.
It describes disbelievers turning away from what they have been warned about.
Denial of the appointed meeting is a broad consequence connection within the passage.
It contrasts revealed truth and faith with disbelief whose appointed end is the Fire.
It joins prophets as bearers and warners with a revealed book of truth amid human disagreement.
The record of deeds at judgment is a general warning consequence.
It states the settled verdict of the Fire for those who disbelieve.
It describes arrogant people rejecting Allah's signs and turning from right guidance.
Taking Satan and his offspring as allies is not a close link to disputing truth.
It merely affirms that truth comes from the Lord.
Directly identifies disbelievers as those who argue concerning Allah's signs.
Rejecting misleaders as aides has only a distant contextual relation.
This statement in Lot's narrative has no useful connection to the focus.
It explains the ordinary human condition of earlier messengers, complementing the focus's statement of their role.
The failure of alleged partners at judgment is not specifically about ridicule or false argument.
Its parable distinguishes enduring truth from vanishing falsehood, answering the focus's truth-falsehood contrast.
Disbelievers explicitly make the messenger an object of mockery.
The certainty of entering the Fire is a broad warning consequence.
Failure to value Allah properly does not supply a specific neighbour relation.
Using falsehood and obstructing Allah's way is only broadly related to resisting truth.
Immediate continuation: it condemns turning away after being reminded of Allah's signs.
It describes the Prophet as sent with truth as a bearer of good news and a warner.
Directly forbids confusing or concealing truth with falsehood.
This isolated assertion of truth lacks a meaningful thematic connection.
Disbelievers mock the messenger by derisively questioning his mission.
It portrays rejection of a confirming revelation that is the truth and hostility toward prophets.
Direct parallel: a disbeliever takes a known sign of Allah in mockery.
It describes knowingly concealing truth after recognizing it.
It warns those who argue about Allah's signs that they have no escape.
Its affirmation of certain truth is too general to be a close neighbour.
It only confirms that the Prophet is among the messengers.
The qiblah command's assertion of truth is unrelated to the focus.
A blessing on the messengers does not engage their mission or its rejection.
The people challenge Abraham's claim of truth by asking whether he is playing.
Directly rebukes disguising and concealing truth with falsehood.
The cattle narrative's acknowledgment of truth is unrelated.
The denial of the messengers by Aad is a broad historical instance of the focus's pattern.
The dispute of Hell's people is unrelated to false worldly disputation against truth.
Taking gods for honor only broadly relates to the unbelievers' rejection of Allah's signs.
It depicts people refusing certainty in Allah's true promise and the Hour.
It rebukes disbelievers who heard Allah's signs yet responded with arrogance.
A warned person dismisses Allah's true promise as tales of the ancients.
Directly asks how those who dispute concerning Allah's signs are turned away.
It sharply contrasts Allah as the truth with the error that follows it.
It contrasts believers recognizing a divine parable as truth with disbelievers objecting to it.
It presents the messenger as sent with guidance and the religion of truth despite polytheist opposition.
The hope for aid from false gods is only an indirect form of false reliance.
The true divine promise and warning against worldly deception form only broad background.
The command concerning Abraham's sanctuary has no relevant connection.
It contrasts the truth brought to deniers with their persistent lying.
The angelic revelation commands warning people of Allah's oneness.
When truth comes, disbelievers call it magic and reject it.
Its account of opponents rejecting truth and expelling the messenger is only contextually related.
The isolated name of the inevitable reality does not form a useful neighbour.
It records affluent townspeople rejecting what their warners were sent with.
It affirms that the Prophet stands on manifest truth without addressing the opponents' response.
It asks deniers whether Allah's signs were recited to them and they rejected them.
It directly contrasts disbelievers following falsehood with believers following truth from their Lord.
It explicitly forbids taking Allah's signs in mockery, though in a legal setting.
It states that conjecture cannot avail against truth, countering false claims against it.
The promise to show signs to impatient people is only a broad warning relation.
It states that the truth came to the people but most of them hated it.
The prohibition on unjust commercial dealings is unrelated.
It explicitly contrasts Allah as the truth with all invoked beings besides Him as falsehood.
The word for glad tidings occurs in a military assurance rather than messengerly warning.
Disbelievers respond to claimed truth with a defiant demand for punishment.
Abraham's compassionate pleading for Lot's people is unrelated.
The description of true believers has no specific relation to the focus.
The incapacity of false gods is only an indirect idolatry connection.
This emphatic affirmation of truth is too general to be useful.
The admission of having been led astray is only a distant consequence of error.
When truth comes, its rejecters label it manifest magic.
Near-verbatim parallel: the Prophet is sent only as a bearer of good news and a warner, with truth.
Deniers accuse the messenger of madness although he brought truth they hate.
It explains that each messenger is sent in his people's language to make the message clear.
Rejoicing in falsehood is not a close relation to disputing divine truth.
The command to warn close kin directly reflects the warning aspect of the mission.
It calls the Qur'an truth and gives its purpose as warning a people without a prior warner.
Professed faith followed by turning away is only broadly related to rejecting the message.
Creation in truth is a theological assertion rather than a response to revelation.
It shows believers expelled for their confession of Allah and affirms divine support for His cause.
It couples creation in truth with disbelief in the meeting with Allah, a distant parallel.
The scene of seized fugitives offers no specific link.
Clear signs are met by disbelievers calling the arriving truth manifest magic.
The legal rulings on emigrant women are unrelated.
It pairs a people's denial of truth with the messenger's limited responsibility toward them.
It consoles the Prophet through earlier messengers who brought proofs and were nevertheless called liars.
It recalls how earlier messengers were mocked and how the mockers were overtaken.
It forbids remaining with people who engage vainly in Allah's signs.
Allah's messengers recounted His signs and warned humans and jinn of their meeting with Him.
It states that messengers come reciting Allah's signs and links response to salvation or loss.
Destroyed generations had received clear proofs from their messengers but persisted in wrongdoing.
Deniers reject what they have not comprehended before its reality reaches them.
Allah establishes the truth by His words despite the criminals' opposition.
Noah's people complain that he has argued with them too extensively and demand the punishment.
Earlier peoples receive clear proofs from messengers yet express doubt about their message.
Disbelieving peoples challenge their messengers and seek to turn them away from inherited worship.
No messenger comes to the criminals without their mocking him.
The Qur'an describes denial entering the hearts of criminals in the pattern of earlier peoples.
Those criminals do not believe despite knowing the precedent of the ancients.
Every community received a messenger commanding worship of Allah and rejection of false gods.
If people turn away, the messenger's duty remains only clear delivery.
Despite many examples in the Qur'an, most people persist in disbelief.
People's objection to a human messenger is identified as what prevented faith after guidance came.
When clear signs are recited, disbelievers counter with worldly-status claims.
It declares punishment for whoever denies the message and turns away.
People hear each new reminder from their Lord while treating it as play.
Wrongdoers secretly dismiss the human messenger and dispute the revelation as sorcery.
Disbelievers successively label the revelation confused dreams, forgery, poetry, and demand a sign.
Some people dispute about Allah without knowledge and follow rebellious devils.
Some people dispute about Allah without knowledge, guidance, or illuminating scripture.
The arrogant disputant turns aside to mislead from Allah's way and faces disgrace.
It recalls earlier nations that denied their messengers before divine punishment came.
The leaders reject their messenger as merely human and deny the possibility of revelation.
The leaders accuse their messenger of inventing a lie about Allah.
Successive messengers are called liars by communities, leading to their destruction.
The disbelievers turn arrogantly away from the Qur'an and speak obscenely about it at night.
It asks whether their rejection results from failing to ponder the word brought to them.
Disbelievers call the Qur'an a falsehood fabricated with outside help.
They dismiss the revelation as tales of the ancients dictated to the Prophet.
They object that the messenger eats food and walks in the markets.
They deride the messenger as bewitched and reject the revealed message.
It answers disbelievers' objection to the Qur'an's gradual revelation.
Every objection they bring is answered with truth and the best explanation.
They have denied the signs, so news of what they ridiculed will reach them.
Noah's people are presented as a people who denied the messengers.
When clear signs come, Pharaoh's people call them manifest magic.
They reject the signs in wrongdoing and arrogance despite inward certainty.
When Moses brings clear signs, his people call them invented magic.
When truth comes, deniers demand the same signs given to Moses and reject both revelations.
Those who will not answer the challenge to bring a truer book are shown to follow desire.
It states that the messenger's obligation is only clear conveyance even when people deny.
Some people believe the revealed Book while others reject its signs.
Those demanding signs are told that signs belong to Allah and the messenger is only a clear warner.
It condemns one who fabricates against Allah or denies truth when it comes.
Earlier communities received clear proofs from their messengers but wronged themselves.
Disbelievers accuse the messenger of fabricating against Allah or of madness.
When clear signs are recited, disbelievers call them a scheme to turn people from ancestral worship.
It consoles the Prophet that messengers before him were also called liars.
Earlier peoples denied messengers who came with clear proofs, scriptures, and illuminating books.
The people reject their messengers as merely human and deny that the Merciful sent anything down.
No messenger comes to people without their mocking him.
People turn away from every sign of their Lord that comes to them.
The Prophet marvels while disbelievers mock.
When disbelievers see a sign, they ridicule it.
Disbelievers marvel at a warner from among themselves and call him a lying magician.
The chiefs dismiss the prophetic call as an invented matter.
They question why the reminder was sent to the Prophet and persist in doubt.
Earlier confederated peoples denied their messengers.
It condemns one who lies about Allah and denies truth when it comes.
The rejected person is told that Allah's signs came, but he denied them arrogantly.
Pharaoh's court calls Moses a lying sorcerer.
Joseph brought clear proofs, yet people remained in doubt and later rejected the messenger.
Those disputing Allah's signs without authority incur great hatred before Allah and believers.
Those disputing Allah's signs without authority are driven only by pride they cannot attain.
Those who deny the Book and the messages sent through messengers will come to know their fate.
The Prophet is a human messenger receiving revelation and warning those who associate partners.
The Prophet warns the rejecters of a thunderbolt like that of Aad and Thamud.
Messengers came to Aad and Thamud with the call to worship Allah alone, but they rejected human messengers.
Disbelievers urge one another not to listen to the Qur'an and to drown it out.
Those who distort Allah's signs are contrasted with those who come secure on the Day of Resurrection.
Falsehood cannot approach the Qur'an from before it or behind it.
The Prophet is told that only what was said to earlier messengers is said to him.
Allah refutes the claim that the Prophet forged a lie and states that He establishes truth by His words.
No prophet came to earlier peoples without their mocking him.
A messenger's call to a better guidance is rejected in favor of ancestral ways.
How can people receive a reminder when a clear messenger has already come to them?
They turn from the messenger and dismiss him as taught or mad.
Allah's signs are recited in truth, and the verse challenges disbelief after Allah and His signs.
It warns every sinful liar who rejects divine truth.
A person hears Allah's signs then persists arrogantly as though he never heard them.
When clear signs are recited, deniers demand that their forefathers be brought back.
It answers the accusation that the Prophet fabricated the Qur'an against Allah.
The Prophet states that he is not unprecedented among messengers and follows revelation only.
A witness recognizes the revelation while deniers remain arrogant.
Disbelievers call the revelation an old falsehood.
Disbelievers are astonished that a warner has come from among them.
They denied truth when it came and are left in confused disorder.
Earlier peoples denied the messengers before the focus's contemporaries.
No messenger came to earlier peoples without their calling him a sorcerer or madman.
When disbelievers see a sign, they turn away and call it continuing magic.
Noah's people denied the messenger, called him mad, and rebuffed him.
Thamud denied the warnings sent to them.
Thamud reject the possibility that guidance could come through a single human messenger.
Lot's people denied the warnings.
When Jesus announces a confirming messenger, disbelievers call the clear message magic.
It condemns forging lies against Allah while being invited to submission.
Disbelievers seek to extinguish Allah's light with their mouths, while Allah completes it.
People reject messengers with clear proofs because they deny that humans can guide them.
The people of Hell admit that a warner came but they called him a liar.
The condemned person is obstinately opposed to Allah's signs.
The disbeliever calls the revealed message inherited magic.
He calls the revelation merely the speech of a human being.
It repeatedly pronounces woe on those who deny the truth.
They persistently denied Allah's signs as lies.
When Allah's signs are recited, the denier calls them tales of the ancients.
